subject: Kindergarten Enrollment and Outreach Strategy
overview: The subcommittee met to restructure the kindergarten enrollment timeline and outreach strategy to better compete with area charter schools. The group proposed moving registration and orientation activities earlier in the year and using city census data for targeted family mailings.

items.title: Review of current kindergarten practices
items.summary: The subcommittee reviewed current kindergarten orientation practices, noting that registration typically begins in March with screenings following in September.

items.title: Comparison with charter schools and neighboring districts
items.summary: Member Graham presented research showing that local charter school lotteries close as early as January 4th, placing the district's March registration at a competitive disadvantage.

items.title: Proposed enrollment timeline and outreach
items.summary: Members discussed a revised timeline to send informational mailings in December, open registration in January, and hold orientation sessions in February.

items.title: Virtual tours and media content
items.summary: The group planned to produce streamlined "day in the life" videos for all elementary schools to provide families with virtual tours while pandemic restrictions prevent in-person visits.

items.title: Utilization of city census data
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent agreed to coordinate with the City Clerk's office to obtain household census data to enable targeted mailings to families with kindergarten-age children.

items.title: Survey of impact and charter school attrition
items.summary: The subcommittee discussed developing an annual survey for families who opt out of the district to understand why they choose charter or parochial schools.
